title: Gauss-elimination (row-rank) method and consistency

pages.heading: Homogeneous Example 4 and parameter Example 5 — beginning

blocks.text: The notebook notes: \(\rho(A)=n\Rightarrow\) unique/trivial solution; \(\rho(A)<n\Rightarrow\) many solutions.

After the written operations \(R_2\to R_2-2R_1\), \(R_3\to R_3-3R_1\), the notebook displays \(\begin{bmatrix}1&2&1\\0&-3&1\\0&-4&-2\end{bmatrix}\), then reaches a third pivot and concludes \(\rho(A)=n\).
5. Find the values of λ and μ so that the system will have (i) unique solution, (ii) many solutions, (iii) no solution
(i) If \(\rho(A)=\rho(A|B)=3\), the system has a unique solution: \(\lambda\ne5\), \(\mu\in\mathbb R\).
(ii) If \(\rho(A)=\rho(A|B)<3\), the system has many solutions: \(\lambda=5\), \(\mu=9\).
(iii) If \(\rho(A)\ne\rho(A|B)\), the system has no solution: the notebook's concluding line gives \(\lambda=5\), \(\mu\ne9\).
